Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

apexog 0.21.0

  • The standard error of every two-step effect (APE and AIE, all first stages, cfinteract, cluster-robust) now adds the direct dependence of the effect on the estimated first-stage parameters through the control function: the influence function is J_beta' psi_beta + J_pi' psi_pi, where versions through 0.20.1 used only the first term (as does Stata’s cfprobit followed by margins). Point estimates are unchanged; standard errors move by about 1% in the validation designs, in either direction. The bivariate-probit engine is unaffected. Mirrors Stata apexog 0.21.0.

apexog 0.20.1

First public release of the R package, a port of the Stata command apexog 0.20.1 that gives the same results.

  • apexog() with method = "uci" (union of confidence intervals over a range for the violation) and method = "ltz" (local-to-zero interval under a prior: normal, uniform, chi-squared, t, gamma, Poisson, an empirical donor, a function, or user-supplied draws), with a sweep over prior widths.
  • Control-function probit with a linear, probit, fractional-probit or Poisson first stage and Murphy-Topel two-step standard errors; recursive bivariate probit for one binary treatment.
  • Average partial effects of every endogenous regressor, or an average interaction effect (continuous by continuous, continuous by binary, binary by binary), including an endogenous treatment interacted with a moderator.
  • The violation on the latent index, in probability points or on the structural latent scale, with the exact probability-scale value of every refit.
  • Robust or cluster-robust standard errors; several instruments and several endogenous regressors.
  • Example data promotion and certification, shipped also as Stata files in inst/extdata.
  • Since Stata apexog 0.20.1 the standard error of an average partial effect with cfinteract includes the sampling variance of the control-function product terms; the R package does the same.
